certificate: CEA Certificate in Business & Freelancing — issued on successful completion of the capstone: a one- page business and freelance plan, a spoken pitch, and a simple financial snapshot A smartphone, free Google tools (Docs, Sheets, Drive, Forms), WhatsApp Business, free Canva, free invoicing templates, and public CAC/FIRS website information Document status Approved for delivery — Version 1.0, October 2026 Companion documents Part 2 — Session Materials (S1–S9), Part 3 — Learner Workbook, Part 6 — Capstone Project About this document. This is the master design document for the CEA Business & Freelancing short course. It explains why the course exists, who it is for, what a graduate can do, how the nine sessions are organised, how learners are assessed, and what they must produce to earn the certificate. It is a blueprint, not teaching notes — lesson plans live in Part2_Sessi
toolset: A smartphone, free Google tools (Docs, Sheets, Drive, Forms), WhatsApp Business, free Canva, free
tools: A smartphone, free Google tools (Docs, Sheets, Drive, Forms), WhatsApp Business, free Canva, free
audience: This course is for absolute beginners. The typical learner is one or more of the following
Aspiring freelancers with a skill — writing, design, barbing, hairdressing, sewing, phone repair, typing, cooking, tutoring, photography — who have never charged for it properly
Micro-business owners and traders — shop owners, market traders, POS operators, artisans — who run on instinct and want structure: prices, quotes, records, registration
Students and NYSC members who want a practical, income-earning start during or after school
Unemployed or underemployed young people who need a real route from skill to first income, without capital for stock or a shop
Side-hustlers with a job who run an evening or weekend service and want to systematise it Family members who manage a family business's money and want clean records
entry_requirements: There is no formal academic entry requirement. To join and benefit fully, a learner needs
A smartphone (Android or iPhone) able to run WhatsApp, a browser and Google apps
Basic smartphone ability — typing, opening apps, taking a photo, recording a voice note. This is assumed, not taught
A free Gmail account (or willingness to create one in S1) for Google Docs, Sheets, Drive, Forms and WhatsApp Business

Willingness to speak, write and role-play in class. Selling and customer conversations are practised aloud. Learners who prefer not to speak publicly may pair with a classmate and submit a written or recorded version; this must be declared to the instructor at the start
One real skill to offer — anything from sewing to typing to cooking to repairing. If a learner believes they have none, that belief is addressed in S1; it is usually untrue
problem: Business & Freelancing is a practical, beginner-level short course that takes a learner from "I have a skill but no customers, no price and no records" to "I can describe my offer, price it, find a customer, manage the job, invoice it and keep simple books."
